title.en: Adding TikTok or a link to a place that is already connected

answer.en: If your place is already connected to a booking platform through Saviku, do not add it again from a TikTok post or another link. Saviku keeps one unit and does not import the link. Share your booking card on TikTok instead, by posting the card image and adding its link to your bio. If your card is not ready, Savi shows you how to finish it. A link from another platform that Saviku can connect means you can add that platform to the same unit. A link from a site Saviku cannot sync is not imported, so block those dates by hand. If you would rather stop using the platform, you can disconnect it and switch to Saviku Direct. Your booking card stays active, and you should hide the platform listing or block its dates to avoid a double booking.

title.en: The same place on more than one platform

answer.en: Connect each platform to the same unit. You keep one booking card and one calendar, and the place counts once. A booking on any platform closes those dates on the others, usually within a minute or two. Each platform keeps its own price, and connecting does not change it, though seasonal prices on some platforms may need checking afterwards. Your stay rules apply everywhere. Remove any iCal calendar links between your platforms first, because they overwrite synced dates. Bookings made on a platform are paid through that platform. Bookings made on your booking card are paid through Saviku and stay in a protected hold until payout.

title.en: Connecting a platform to a place you added from TikTok or a link

answer.en: Choose Connect a platform in My Property and pick your place. Saviku links the platform to your existing unit and does not create a new one. Your booking card, its link and your TikTok posts stay the same, and the place still counts once. Your dates and bookings are kept, and any dates already booked in Saviku close on the new platform. Your platform price and your booking card price stay separate. Your card stays open for bookings while you connect.

title.en: Your booking card price and your platform prices

answer.en: Your booking card price is separate from your platform prices. Direct bookings avoid platform fees, so you can set a lower price on your card. Changing your card price never changes a platform price. To change a platform price, open Pricing, choose Platform prices, and confirm the change for that platform. Your availability is always shared, so a booked night closes everywhere.

title.en: How does the 48-Hour Booking Protection work?

answer.en:
Secure Booking: Your payment is processed through Saviku’s payment provider, allocated to your booking and not paid directly to the host at collection.

Protection Window: You have 48 hours after scheduled check-in to cancel or report a material problem.

Host Payout: If no eligible cancellation or dispute is open, Saviku instructs the provider to pay the verified host after that window, subject to provider availability.

Guest Guarantee: If any critical listing or access issues occur, you are covered under Saviku’s booking protection policy.

answer.en: A protected stay is a booking made and paid for through a Saviku booking card. Every payment through Saviku is protected. Your payment goes through Saviku's payment provider and is allocated to your booking. It is not paid directly to the host when you book. It stays in a protected hold until the protection window ends, so there is time to report a problem. Bookings made on Airbnb, Booking.com or another platform follow that platform's own rules.

title.en: How does a protected stay work?

answer.en: First, the guest picks dates on the booking card. Depending on the host's setting, the dates are accepted from the calendar or the host approves the request. Next, the guest pays and the payment stays in a protected hold. The guest then has 48 hours after scheduled check-in to cancel or report a material problem. If no eligible cancellation or dispute is open after that window, Saviku instructs the provider to pay the verified host, minus the disclosed service fee. If a dispute is raised, a Saviku reviewer decides it under the stays terms.

title.en: What do the badges on a booking card mean?

answer.en: Every booking card shows Protected with a lock icon, because every payment through Saviku is protected. Beside it, a card can show one status badge. A listing connected to a platform or TikTok shows a badge such as Airbnb Verified or TikTok Verified until its first guest confirms the stay. It then moves to Saviku Direct, with a shield icon. A listing created from scratch on Saviku can show Listing Verified instead, if the host took an optional photo inside the place. Badges tell you what has been confirmed about a listing. They do not change your protection.
